He asked her for a drink. Jews and Samaritans didn't even talk. 💧 John 4

Jesus, “wearied with his journey,” sat on Jacob's well and asked a Samaritan woman for water. Then He offered her something better: “whosoever drinketh of the water that I shall give him shall never thirst” (John 4:14). He knew her whole story, and told her plainly: “I that speak unto thee am he” (John 4:26). She left her waterpot and brought the whole city.

What would you have said to Him at that well? 👇

God said go. He ran the other way. 🐋 Jonah 1-3

Jonah paid the fare for a ship to Tarshish “from the presence of the Lord.” A storm, a lot that fell on him, and “the Lord had prepared a great fish to swallow up Jonah” (Jonah 1:17). From the belly of the fish he prayed: “Salvation is of the Lord” (Jonah 2:9). Then “the word of the Lord came unto Jonah the second time” (Jonah 3:1), and all of Nineveh believed God.

Have you ever run from something God asked you to do? 👇

End your day with Him. 🌙📖

A 5-step night routine, faith edition: lamp on, notifications off. Read one chapter, just one. Make it stick with one line in your journal. Hand Him your tomorrow in prayer. Then phone down, lights off. “I will both lay me down in peace, and sleep: for thou, Lord, only makest me dwell in safety” (Psalm 4:8).

Which step do you skip the most? Comment 1 to 5 👇

He wasted it all. His father ran to him. 🏃‍♂️ Luke 15:11-32

The younger son took his share and “wasted his substance with riotous living.” Broke and feeding pigs, “he came to himself” and headed home. “But when he was yet a great way off, his father saw him, and had compassion, and ran, and fell on his neck, and kissed him” (Luke 15:20). “For this my son was dead, and is alive again; he was lost, and is found” (Luke 15:24).

Are you more like the younger brother or the older one? 👇

Walking in uncalled could get her killed. She went anyway. 👑 Esther 3-8

Haman plotted to destroy all the Jews in one day. Mordecai asked Esther: “who knoweth whether thou art come to the kingdom for such a time as this?” (Esther 4:14). Going to the king uncalled meant death unless he held out the golden sceptre. Her answer: “and if I perish, I perish” (Esther 4:16). On the third day, the king held out the sceptre.

What's your “such a time as this” right now? 👇
